newsitem.title: USA: Calif. order electric utility rate unbundling.
newsitem.headline: Calif. order electric utility rate unbundling.

text.p: The California Public Utilities Commission voted Friday to order separation, known as unbundling, of what traditionally have been services only provided by electric utiities.

The separation is aimed at giving consumers information they can use to choose among providers and services as the state heads toward allowing open competition between electricity suppliers on January 1.

The three major components on electric bills will be generation, transmission and distribution. Other components include public purpose programs, energy efficiency programs, low-income services, the competition transition charge (CTC) and nuclear decommissioning.
Except for the commodity cost of electricity, which may vary between suppliers, customers will pay a fixed rate for each component.
The CPUC decided the utilities will have until June 1, 1998, to create fully unbundled bills.
Starting January, utilities can continue to sell electricity but will be competing with other sellers.

An independent entity, the Power Exchange (PX), will set the price of electricity, which will be a weighted average of day-ahead and hour-ahead prices, adjusted for administrative costs, settlements and other fees.

Utilities will continue to own their transmission systems but will turn operation of them over to an independent entity, the Independent System Operator (ISO), which will be regulated by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

The CPUC said it also decided Friday to reduce utilities' distribution revenue requirements from what the companies had proposed because they included various costs that should instead be recovered through their generation revenue requirement.

The commission said the approved distribution revenues are: $1.67 billion for Edison International's Southern California Edison Co, $1.95 billion for PG&E Corp's Pacific Gas & Electric Co, and $501.6 million for Enova Corp's San Diego Gas & Electric Co.

The CPUC said it is now reviewing SDG&E's performance-based rate making mechanism, PG&E must file a general rate case later this year and it will evaluate Edison's performance-based rate making mechanism in 1999.
As a result, the commission deferred adjusting the utilities total authorized revenue until these cases have been decided.
